title: Dua passage dengan timer
title_target: Reading — two full passages under exam conditions
goal: Menyelesaikan dua passage penuh (20 soal) dalam 22 menit tanpa kamus, dengan urutan kerja yang sama persis seperti yang akan kamu pakai di ruang ujian — lalu membaca skornya sebagai peta: bagian mana yang sudah siap dan bagian mana yang harus diulang.
bekal: menjaga ritme 11 menit per passage tanpa melihat jam tiap 30 detik
memutuskan dalam 20 detik pertama apakah sebuah passage dikerjakan sekarang atau dilompati
mengisi lembar jawab per passage, bukan per soal, tanpa salah geser baris

sections.title: Ini bukan unit belajar — ini gladi bersih

blocks.text: Unit 12 sampai 14 mengajarkan tiap tipe soal Reading satu per satu. Unit ini menggabungkan semuanya dalam kondisi yang paling mirip ruang ujian: dua passage, dua puluh soal, satu timer. Tidak ada strategi baru di sini. Yang diuji adalah apakah strategi yang sudah kamu pelajari tetap jalan ketika waktu terus berkurang dan passage kedua sudah menunggu.

Section 3 memberi 55 menit untuk lima passage — **11 menit per passage**, sudah termasuk membaca dan menjawab sepuluh soal. Angka ini terdengar longgar sampai kamu mencobanya. Kebanyakan siswa yang gagal di Reading bukan karena tidak paham teksnya, melainkan karena menghabiskan 16 menit di passage pertama, 14 di kedua, lalu menebak setengah soal passage kelima. Skor 550+ butuh sekitar 40 dari 50 soal benar, dan itu mustahil kalau satu passage terlantar.
Ritme 11 menit hanya bisa dijaga kalau urutan kerjamu tetap sama di tiap passage. Urutan yang disarankan modul ini — dan yang akan kamu pakai untuk dua passage di bawah — begini:

items: **Menit 0–1: baca kalimat pertama tiap paragraf**, plus kalimat terakhir paragraf terakhir. Jangan baca seluruh passage dulu. Tujuannya cuma tahu topiknya dan apa isi tiap paragraf secara kasar. Kamu belum menjawab apa pun.

**Menit 1–2: jawab soal main idea/purpose** — biasanya soal nomor 1. Setelah membaca kalimat pertama tiap paragraf, kamu sudah punya cukup bahan. Kalau masih ragu, tandai jawaban sementara dan kembali lagi di akhir.

**Menit 2–9: kerjakan soal urut dari atas.** Soal Reading TOEFL ITP mengikuti urutan paragraf: soal 2–3 biasanya tentang paragraf 1, soal 4–5 paragraf 2, dan seterusnya. Baca paragraf yang dirujuk dengan teliti *baru saat soalnya menuntut*, bukan sebelumnya. Soal vocabulary dan reference dikerjakan di tempat, dari kalimat sumbernya.

**Menit 9–11: soal NOT/EXCEPT dan organisasi dikerjakan terakhir.** Dua tipe ini memaksa kamu membaca satu paragraf penuh atau seluruh passage. Kalau dikerjakan urut, mereka memakan waktu yang seharusnya untuk soal detail yang lebih murah. Pada saat kamu sampai di sini, kamu sudah membaca hampir seluruh teks, jadi keduanya jadi jauh lebih cepat.

blocks.text: Lima passage tidak sama sulitnya, dan urutannya tidak diatur dari mudah ke sulit. Kalau setelah membaca kalimat pertama tiap paragraf kamu benar-benar tidak menangkap topiknya — biasanya passage sains dengan istilah teknis bertumpuk — **lewati sekarang**, kerjakan passage berikutnya, dan kembali kalau ada waktu. Passage yang sulit untukmu dikerjakan terakhir, bukan pertama, karena kalau waktu habis di sana kerugianmu paling kecil: soal-soalnya toh sudah kamu tebak. Yang tidak boleh terjadi adalah waktu habis di passage yang sebenarnya mudah.

Melompat hanya aman kalau kamu disiplin dengan lembar jawab. Aturannya: **isi lembar jawab per passage, bukan per soal.** Lingkari jawaban di buku soal selama mengerjakan sepuluh soal, lalu pindahkan sepuluh jawaban itu sekaligus ke lembar jawab sebelum berpindah passage. Ini memakan 20–30 detik, tapi menghilangkan kesalahan hari tes yang paling menyakitkan: salah geser baris, sehingga jawaban soal 24 tertulis di baris 25 dan seterusnya sampai akhir. Kalau kamu melompati satu passage, sepuluh baris di lembar jawab dibiarkan kosong dulu — dan kamu tahu persis baris mana karena kamu berpindah per blok sepuluh.

blocks.title: Sebelum mulai: aturan latihan ini
items: **Timer 22 menit** untuk dua passage dan dua puluh soal — 11 menit per passage. Pasang timer sebelum membuka passage pertama, dan patuhi batas 11 menitnya: begitu 11 menit pertama habis, pindah ke Passage 2 walaupun Passage 1 belum selesai. Soal yang tersisa ditebak.

**Tanpa kamus, tanpa ketuk kata.** Reader ini bisa menampilkan arti kata dengan sekali ketuk, dan di tes asli fitur itu tidak ada. Baru setelah kedua latihan selesai dan kuncinya keluar, kembalilah ke passage dan ketuk kata yang tadi menghambatmu.
**Kerjakan Latihan 1 (Passage 1) lalu Latihan 2 (Passage 2), jangan dicampur.** Isi jawaban di reader per latihan, seperti memindahkan satu blok ke lembar jawab.
**Catat waktumu per passage**, bukan cuma totalnya. Kalau Passage 1 memakan 14 menit dan Passage 2 hanya 8, kamu belum mengatur ritme — kamu cuma beruntung Passage 2 lebih mudah.

blocks.text: Setelah selesai, jangan langsung membaca pembahasan. Lihat dulu kunci jawaban, hitung skormu dari 20, lalu baca kotak *Cara membaca hasilmu* di ujung pembahasan. Baru setelah itu bedah soal yang salah satu per satu.
Mulai timer. Sebelas menit untuk passage ini dan sepuluh soal Latihan 1.

paragraphs.text: In the early decades of the twentieth century, farmers on the southern Great Plains of the United States enjoyed a period of unusual prosperity. Rainfall was generous, wheat prices climbed during the First World War, and new gasoline-powered tractors allowed a single family to plow far more land than horses ever could. Between 1910 and 1930, millions of acres of native grassland in Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, Colorado, and New Mexico were turned over to wheat. Few people at the time considered that the deep-rooted grasses being removed had held the region's thin topsoil in place for thousands of years.

The consequences became apparent when the rain stopped. Beginning in 1931, the Plains entered a drought that would last, with brief interruptions, for most of the decade. Crops failed, and with no grass to anchor it, the dry soil simply blew away. Enormous dust storms, which residents called "black blizzards," rolled across the region, burying fences, choking livestock, and turning midday into night. The worst of these struck on April 14, 1935, a date remembered as Black Sunday, when a wall of dust thousands of feet high swept from the Dakotas to Texas. Journalists soon gave the affected area a name that stuck: the Dust Bowl.

For families who had borrowed money to buy land and machinery, ruin came quickly. Unable to pay their debts, many abandoned their farms altogether. During the 1930s roughly 2.5 million people left the Plains states, one of the largest migrations in American history. Several hundred thousand of them headed west to California, drawn by handbills promising work in the state's orchards and cotton fields. Whatever their state of origin, Californians labeled them "Okies," a term that was rarely intended as a compliment. Most found only seasonal labor at low wages and lived in roadside camps, a situation that John Steinbeck would later describe in his novel The Grapes of Wrath.

The federal government responded with measures that permanently changed American agriculture. In 1935 Congress created the Soil Conservation Service, which paid farmers to plant grass on damaged land, to plow along the contours of hills rather than in straight lines, and to leave the remains of harvested crops in the fields to protect the surface. Rows of trees known as shelterbelts were planted across the Plains to slow the wind. When normal rainfall returned in 1939, the land had begun to recover — and the lesson that soil, once lost, is not easily replaced had been learned at enormous cost.

blocks.title: Plate Tectonics and the Ring of Fire

paragraphs.text: Until the middle of the twentieth century, most geologists believed that the continents had always occupied their present positions. In 1912 the German scientist Alfred Wegener had suggested otherwise, pointing out that the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like pieces of a puzzle and that identical fossils appeared on both sides of the Atlantic. His idea of "continental drift" was widely dismissed, however, because he could not explain what force might push whole continents across the globe.

The explanation arrived in the 1960s, when surveys of the ocean floor revealed long underwater mountain chains where new crust was continuously being formed. Scientists concluded that the Earth's outer shell is not a single piece but a mosaic of roughly a dozen large plates and several smaller ones. These plates rest on the hotter, softer rock beneath them and move at a rate of a few centimeters per year — about as fast as human fingernails grow. Where two plates pull apart, molten rock rises to fill the gap; where they collide, one plate is usually forced beneath the other in a process called subduction. This theory, known as plate tectonics, unified ideas about earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain building that had previously seemed unrelated.

Nowhere are the effects of subduction more visible than along the edges of the Pacific Ocean. A horseshoe-shaped belt some 40,000 kilometers long, stretching from the southern tip of South America up the west coast of North America, across to Japan, and down through the Philippines, Indonesia, and New Zealand, contains about three quarters of the world's active volcanoes. Roughly ninety percent of the planet's earthquakes occur there as well. Geographers call this belt the Ring of Fire, although it is not a single feature but a series of separate boundaries where oceanic plates are sinking beneath their neighbors.

The sinking plate carries water-rich sediments into the hot interior, where they lower the melting point of the surrounding rock. The resulting magma rises to the surface and builds the steep, explosive volcanoes typical of the region, such as Mount St. Helens in Washington State, which erupted violently in 1980. The same plate movements produce the largest earthquakes ever recorded, including the magnitude 9.5 event that struck Chile in 1960. For the millions of people who live along the Ring of Fire, understanding plate tectonics is not an academic exercise but a matter of daily safety.

exercises.prompt: Questions 1–10. Passage 1: The Dust Bowl. Choose the best answer to each question. Batas 11 menit — isi semua nomor sebelum pindah ke Latihan 2.
items: What does the passage mainly discuss? (A) The development of the gasoline-powered tractor (B) The lives of migrant workers in California (C) The history of the Soil Conservation Service (D) The causes and consequences of an environmental disaster on the Great Plains ____
The word *generous* in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to (A) plentiful (B) unpredictable (C) expensive (D) kind ____

According to paragraph 1, which of the following contributed to the expansion of wheat farming? (A) Government loans to farmers (B) The introduction of new tractors (C) A decline in the number of horses (D) The discovery of deep-rooted grasses ____
The word *it* in paragraph 2 refers to (A) rain (B) grass (C) soil (D) drought ____

According to paragraph 2, Black Sunday was (A) the most severe dust storm of the period (B) the day the drought began (C) the first time journalists used the name Dust Bowl (D) a storm that affected only Texas ____
The word *ruin* in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to (A) disease (B) boredom (C) violence (D) financial disaster ____

According to paragraph 3, all of the following are true of the migrants who went to California EXCEPT: (A) They were attracted by advertisements for work. (B) They all came from Oklahoma. (C) They usually earned little money. (D) Many of them lived in temporary camps. ____

It can be inferred from paragraph 3 that the term *Okies* (A) was used mostly by people from Oklahoma themselves (B) was invented by John Steinbeck (C) was generally used in a negative way (D) referred only to farm owners ____

Why does the author mention *shelterbelts* in paragraph 4? (A) To explain why rainfall returned in 1939 (B) To criticize the Soil Conservation Service (C) To show that trees grew naturally on the Plains (D) To give an example of a measure taken to reduce wind damage ____

According to paragraph 4, the Soil Conservation Service encouraged farmers to do which of the following? (A) Buy more land (B) Plant grass on damaged land (C) Plow in straight lines (D) Clear the fields completely after harvest ____

exercises.prompt: Questions 11–20. Passage 2: Plate Tectonics and the Ring of Fire. Choose the best answer to each question. Batas 11 menit.
items: What is the main purpose of the passage? (A) To describe the life and work of Alfred Wegener (B) To compare volcanoes in different parts of the world (C) To argue that earthquakes cannot be predicted (D) To explain the theory of plate tectonics and one of its consequences ____

According to paragraph 1, why did most scientists not accept Wegener's idea? (A) His fossil evidence was incorrect. (B) He was not a trained geologist. (C) He could not explain what moved the continents. (D) The coastlines did not actually match. ____
The word *dismissed* in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to (A) rejected (B) discussed (C) published (D) forgotten ____
The word *them* in paragraph 2 refers to (A) scientists (B) plates (C) mountain chains (D) surveys ____

According to paragraph 2, which of the following is true of the plates? (A) They move faster than fingernails grow. (B) There are exactly twelve of them. (C) They were first identified by Wegener. (D) They rest on softer rock. ____

Why does the author mention human fingernails in paragraph 2? (A) To show how slowly the plates move (B) To explain how subduction works (C) To describe the composition of the Earth's crust (D) To compare the Earth with the human body ____
The word *unified* in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to (A) replaced (B) brought together (C) questioned (D) simplified ____
According to paragraph 3, the Ring of Fire includes all of the following EXCEPT (A) the west coast of North America (B) Japan (C) the coast of Africa (D) New Zealand ____

Empat paragraf: kemakmuran dan pembukaan lahan (sebab) → kekeringan dan badai debu → migrasi → tanggapan pemerintah. Hanya (D) yang memayungi semuanya. (A), (B), (C) masing-masing cuma satu paragraf — pengecoh klasik soal main idea: detail yang benar tapi terlalu sempit.
A
*Rainfall was generous* sejajar dengan *wheat prices climbed* dan *prosperity*: hujan **berlimpah**. (D) *kind* adalah arti *generous* untuk orang, bukan untuk hujan — jebakan arti kamus pertama.
B

*new gasoline-powered tractors allowed a single family to plow far more land*. (C) memutarbalik: kuda tidak berkurang, traktor mengalahkannya. (D) memakai kata dari teks (*deep-rooted grasses*) tapi rumput itu dihilangkan, bukan ditemukan.

*with no grass to anchor it, the dry soil simply blew away*. Yang perlu ditambat (*anchor*) adalah tanah, dan *the dry soil* muncul tepat setelahnya sebagai subjek. Uji: ganti *it* dengan *the soil* — kalimatnya masuk akal; ganti dengan *grass* — tidak.
A

*The worst of these struck on April 14, 1935, a date remembered as Black Sunday*. *The worst of these* = badai debu paling parah. (B) salah: kekeringan mulai 1931. (D) bertentangan: *from the Dakotas to Texas*.
D
Konteksnya *families who had borrowed money … unable to pay their debts*: kehancuran keuangan. (A) dan (C) tidak dibahas sama sekali.
B

*Whatever their state of origin, Californians labeled them Okies* — justru menegaskan mereka datang dari BERBAGAI negara bagian. (A) = *drawn by handbills promising work*; (C) = *low wages*; (D) = *roadside camps*. Semua ada, kecuali (B).
C
*a term that was rarely intended as a compliment* — jarang dimaksudkan sebagai pujian → biasanya merendahkan. (B) salah: Steinbeck menggambarkan kondisinya, bukan menciptakan istilahnya.
D

Kalimatnya: *shelterbelts were planted across the Plains to slow the wind* — satu dari beberapa langkah perlindungan tanah di paragraf 4. (A) mengarang sebab-akibat: hujan kembali karena musim, bukan karena pohon.
B

*paid farmers to plant grass on damaged land*. (C) dan (D) adalah kebalikan persis dari teks: *along the contours … rather than in straight lines* dan *leave the remains of harvested crops in the fields*.

rows: D
Paragraf 1–2 membangun teorinya, paragraf 3–4 menerapkannya pada Cincin Api — teori plus satu akibatnya. (A) cuma paragraf 1; (B) tidak ada perbandingan antarwilayah; (C) tidak pernah dibahas.
C

*because he could not explain what force might push whole continents across the globe*. (B) masuk akal di dunia nyata (Wegener memang ahli meteorologi), tapi teks tidak menyebutnya — tipikal pengecoh inferensi liar.
A

*widely dismissed, however, because …* — kata *however* mengontraskan dengan bukti yang tampak kuat sebelumnya, dan alasannya menyusul: ide itu **ditolak**. (D) *forgotten* terlalu jauh; ide yang dilupakan tidak butuh alasan.
B

*These plates rest on the hotter, softer rock beneath them and move …* — subjek kalimatnya *these plates*; batuan lunak ada *di bawah lempeng*. (C) *mountain chains* ada di kalimat sebelumnya, pengecoh jarak.
D

*These plates rest on the hotter, softer rock beneath them*. (A) bertentangan: *about as fast as* (sama, bukan lebih). (B) *roughly a dozen* bukan *exactly twelve*. (C) bertentangan dengan paragraf 1–2: Wegener mengusulkan drift, lempengnya baru dikenali 1960-an.
A

Perbandingan dengan kuku dipasang tepat setelah *a few centimeters per year* — untuk memberi bayangan betapa lambatnya. Soal *why does the author mention* selalu dijawab dari fungsi kalimatnya di paragraf, bukan dari isi perbandingannya.
B

*unified ideas … that had previously seemed unrelated* — yang tadinya terpisah dijadikan satu. Kontras *unrelated* adalah petunjuk utamanya. (D) *simplified* menggoda tapi teks tidak bicara tentang menyederhanakan.
C

Daftar di paragraf 3: *South America … west coast of North America … Japan … the Philippines, Indonesia, and New Zealand*. Afrika tidak ada — dan memang tidak berbatasan dengan Pasifik. Afrika hanya muncul di paragraf 1, soal garis pantai.
A

*Geographers call this belt the Ring of Fire, although it is not a single feature but a series of separate boundaries*. *Although … not a single feature* = namanya menyiratkan satu cincin, kenyataannya bukan → agak menyesatkan. (D) terlalu jauh: tidak ada yang menolak namanya.
B

*water-rich sediments … lower the melting point of the surrounding rock* = batuan meleleh pada suhu yang lebih rendah. (A) kebalikan: interiornya panas dan tetap panas. (D) tidak disebut; yang naik adalah magma.

blocks.title: Cara membaca hasilmu
items: **16–20 benar dalam 22 menit: kamu siap 550+ di Section 3.** Ritme dan strateginya sudah jadi kebiasaan. Pertahankan dengan satu passage berwaktu per hari sampai hari tes, dan kerjakan tes lengkap di Simulasi minimal dua kali supaya terbiasa dengan lima passage berturut-turut.

**12–15 benar: strategi sudah ada, eksekusinya belum stabil.** Lihat tipe soal mana yang bocor. Kalau yang salah kebanyakan vocabulary/reference, ulang **Unit 13**; kalau NOT/EXCEPT, inference, atau organisasi, ulang **Unit 14**. Lalu kerjakan unit ini lagi seminggu kemudian — targetnya 16+.

**Di bawah 12: ulang Unit 12–14 berurutan** sebelum menyentuh passage berwaktu lagi, dan tambahkan bacaan harian: satu artikel bahasa Inggris 300–400 kata per hari (ensiklopedia, majalah sains populer), dibaca sekali tanpa kamus lalu tulis satu kalimat main idea-nya. Masalahmu kemungkinan bukan strategi tapi kecepatan membaca, dan itu hanya naik lewat jam terbang.
**Apa pun skormu, cek waktunya.** Skor 17 dengan 30 menit belum siap; skor 14 dengan 21 menit lebih dekat ke target daripada yang terlihat, karena waktu lebih sulit diperbaiki daripada ketelitian.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat dari dua passage ini
items: Empat soal EXCEPT/NOT dan organisasi (7, 9, 18, 19) adalah soal yang paling mahal waktunya. Kalau kamu mengerjakannya urut, kamu membaca paragraf 3 dua kali. Dengan urutan yang disarankan, kamu membacanya sekali dan menjawab dua soal sekaligus.

Soal 12 dan 15 memakai pengecoh yang sama: **fakta yang benar di dunia nyata tapi tidak ada di teks**. Di Reading TOEFL ITP, jawaban selalu dari passage, bukan dari pengetahuanmu — bahkan kalau pengetahuanmu benar.
Dua soal reference (4, 14) bisa dijawab dalam 15 detik dengan satu uji: ganti kata gantinya dengan tiap pilihan, baca kalimatnya. Hanya satu yang masuk akal secara tata bahasa DAN makna.
